# Python

Full rules, evidence and examples: `common/languages/python.md`.

- PY-01 must: Lint and format with ruff only, through pre-commit (`ruff --fix`, `ruff-format`) and `ruff check .` in CI; add no black, isort, flake8 or pylint. [tool:ruff]
  Good: `.pre-commit-config.yaml` with the `ruff --fix` and `ruff-format` hooks and `ruff check .` in CI.
  Bad: a `black` hook next to a `flake8` hook.
- PY-02 prefer: Use ruff defaults without a `[tool.ruff]` section; a stricter `ruff.toml` (`E W F B I UP`, 120 columns, a reason comment on each ignore) applies only to script collections. [tool:ruff]
- PY-03 must: Manage projects with poetry (`pyproject.toml`, `poetry.lock`) and pin the Python constraint to the supported minor (`>=3.14,<3.15`); follow the Home Assistant minimum Python for integrations.
  Good: `python = ">=3.14,<3.15"` in `pyproject.toml` next to a committed `poetry.lock`.
  Bad: `python = "*"` or a `requirements.txt` as the only manifest.
- PY-04 must: Python: set `fail_under = 95` and `show_missing = true` for PRIN-37, and run pytest with `--strict-markers --cov=<package>`. [tool:pytest-cov]
  Good: `fail_under = 95` and `show_missing = true` under `[tool.coverage.report]`; `addopts = "--strict-markers --cov=mypkg"`.
  Bad: `fail_under = 80` or a pytest run without `--cov`.
- PY-05 prefer: Use no `pragma: no mutate` blocks; remove existing ones when you touch the file. Observed: run mutmut in CI and keep log lines out of mutation with a coverage exclusion and `do_not_mutate_patterns`.
- PY-06 prefer: Group tests in a `Test<Class>` class without a base class, name methods `test_<behavior>`, add an `__init__.py` per folder, and give no docstring to test methods; a module docstring is one line.
- PY-07 lean: In constructor tests assert every attribute, test defaults in a separate test, and test `__str__` with the full expected string.
- PY-08 prefer: Test async code with pytest-asyncio and `aioresponses`; use the Home Assistant pytest plugin for integrations; keep fakes in `tests/helpers.py` and fixtures in `conftest.py`.
- PY-09 lean: Prove with a dedicated test that secrets never reach logs, repr or exceptions, using a recognizable fake token and `caplog`.
- PY-10 prefer: One class per module, named in snake_case after the concept; group modules in packages by kind (`data/`, `device/`, `enum/`, `exception/`, `utils/`); every folder has an `__init__.py` with a one-line docstring.
- PY-11 prefer: Order imports standard library, third party, local; use relative imports inside the package and `collections.abc` for ABCs.
- PY-12 prefer: Run pyright in CI of new Python projects. Observed: annotate public signatures with modern syntax (`X | None`, `list[str]`), never `Optional` or `typing.List`.
- PY-13 must: Give every module, class and public function a docstring: a one-line summary with a period, then one `name: description` line per parameter, even an obvious one, without `Args:` and without types; this API documentation overrides PRIN-05 and PRIN-14.
  Good: `identifier: the device identifier to cancel the command for`
  Bad: an `Args:` block with types.
- PY-14 prefer: Close a multi-line docstring on the last text line, in all Python code.
- PY-15 prefer: Refer to methods in docstrings as `::name` and state behavioral contracts (raised errors, state kept on failure) in the docstring, not in comments.
- PY-16 prefer: End exception names in `Exception`, not `Error`. Observed: use snake_case modules and functions, PascalCase classes, UPPER_SNAKE constants in `const.py`, and a leading underscore to mark internals (`_helper`, `self._client`); dunder methods (`__str__`) and `_LOGGER = logging.getLogger(__name__)` are fine.
- PY-18 must: Python: write log messages lowercase without a period in new or substantially rewritten code and fix existing ones when you touch them (PRIN-32).
  Good: `"adding %s hella_onyx light entities"`
- PY-19 lean: Example only, not a rule: onyx-client returns `None` or `False` and logs on an unusable API response, and raises only for rejected credentials or invalid configuration.
- PY-20 prefer: Catch specific exception types, chain with `raise ... from ex`, and use broad `except Exception` only at a task boundary with a logged reason.
- PY-21 prefer: Prefer plain literals and `.get("key")`: `[]` not `list()`, no redundant `None` default, `is None` checks.
- PY-22 lean: Example only, not a rule: onyx-client v12 uses `asyncio.timeout` and async iteration and leaves the session and loop to the caller.
- PY-23 prefer: In integrations follow the upstream Home Assistant developer documentation.
- PY-24 prefer: Publish libraries with `poetry-core`, trusted publishing and release-please; an integration uses `package-mode = false` and pins the library version in `manifest.json`.
- PY-25 lean: Example only, not a rule: the deprecated node-red backup_restore CLI uses `click` with one function per command.
- PY-26 prefer: Use `@dataclass` for new value objects that compare all fields; keep plain classes for entities that compare by identifier or run logic in `__init__`; leave existing classes unchanged.

Avoid (AI-Era Artifacts):

- `Args:` and `Returns:` docstrings, and long explanatory docstrings, beyond summary plus parameters.
- `pragma: no mutate` blocks around log calls.
- Comments above every constant in new code beyond reason or unit.
